previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with type 2 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, peripheral vascular disease, and coronary artery disease was admitted for hyperglycemia with blood sugars in the 400s and a history of insulin sensitivity. He had recently undergone a procedure on his right saphenous stent and had a poorly healing leg ulcer. Evaluation showed stable cardiac status with no acute ischemia, and his diabetes was deemed poorly controlled due to recent stress and disease progression. Insulin therapy was initiated with 75-25 insulin at 5 units twice daily, and the patient was educated on self-administration and glucose monitoring. He responded well with fasting sugars in the 140s and daytime levels in the 100s, without hypoglycemia. Hemodialysis was completed, achieving dry weight, and his leg wound was managed with wet-to-dry dressings. The patient was discharged home with a structured insulin regimen, medication adjustments, and follow-up appointments with a diabetologist, nutritionist, vascular surgeon, and orthopedics.

renal disease.  Evaluate for acute process.

TWO VIEWS OF THE CHEST:  There has been prior sternotomy and CABG, with intact
midline sternal wires and numerous vascular clips.  A right chest dual-lead
pacing device remains in unchanged position.  Moderate cardiomegaly is
unchanged with no evidence of congestive heart failure.  There is chronic
right basilar atelectasis and small right pleural effusion.  There is no new
consolidation.  Osseous structures and soft tissues appear unremarkable except
for mild degenerative change.
